Food A+ but the service just an A.
Aug 2026 • Friends
Dropped in on a Tuesday night with no reservation...no problem. We could have had a tsble outside right awsy but with storms about we opted for inside. Only a few minutes later we were in.
The lady at the door could have been a little friendlier but not a major problem. Once seated we were given only one menu between three of us but when we asked for one more it was there in a flash. 
Onto the eating part of the night and everything was amazing. The menu is extensive. Journey to many parts of Vietnam via it. Fantastic food served quickly and well and truly met all expectations.
If you are in Hanoi this is a must for one of your nights.

“Michelin Selected” authentic Vietnamese restaurant
May 2026 • Friends
Quán Ăn Ngon in Hanoi is a bustling, well-loved restaurant recognized by Michelin, serving a variety of authentic Vietnamese dishes that are both affordable and expertly prepared. 

Set in a charming colonial villa, it is especially renowned for bánh xèo—Vietnamese pancakes—and Bún chả, a Northern Hanoi specialty featuring charcoal-grilled pork served with a light, savory-sweet broth, cold rice vermicelli noodles, and fresh herbs. The menu also includes grilled dishes, fried rice, veggies, seafood, spring rolls, and regional specialties. Its vibrant, open-kitchen courtyard atmosphere makes it a favorite among locals and tourists alike. 

All the dishes we tried were fantastic, prepared with fresh ingredients and well-balanced flavors. We truly enjoyed the dining experience at this lively restaurant, which left a lasting memory.

Without high expectations and yet disappointed
Apr 2026 • Friends
The restaurant left us with a dodgy impression. For a Michelin-winning house, the volume in the room and the lack of noise insulation were surprisingly disturbing, so a relaxed stay was hardly possible.
Organizationally, the process did not seem convincing either. The menu was unusually large, the food was not served at the same time, and the cutlery was initially completely missing from the table. It was also particularly disappointing that the starter only came after the main course.
Culinarily, the food was not completely convincing overall. Simple dishes were noticeably overpriced and not particularly salient in taste. 
Positively remembered, however, was the juicy and tender beef from the skewer, which was clearly the highlight of the stay.
Overall, the visit for an excellent restaurant did not seem coherent enough to meet expectations.
